summary:
AgroGeo Sphere is a NASA Earth-observation-powered agricultural decision-support platform designed to address the growing disconnect between Pakistan's changing agroclimatic conditions and farmers' access to actionable agricultural intelligence. Recognising that agriculture sustains 23.5% of Pakistan's GDP and over 37% of its workforce, our project targets a structural challenge: crop decisions are frequently made without an integrated understanding of historical environmental conditions, water availability and alternative cropping systems.

Piloted in Jaranwala, Faisalabad, the platform combines Landsat vegetation observations, GPM precipitation records, NASA POWER climate data and regional agricultural evidence. Its Field Intelligence interface contextualises land conditions, while farmer-provided information grounds the analysis in individual field circumstances. Precision Lab compares three crop rotations—fodder, pulses and fallow—against water suitability, seasonal compatibility, soil-cover duration and nutrient-cycling potential. CropMaster AI translates these findings into accessible, evidence-grounded explanations.

Our vision is to democratise agricultural intelligence: reducing information asymmetry, supporting more resource-conscious decisions, protecting farmers' livelihoods and strengthening long-term food-system resilience. Rather than replacing agricultural expertise, AgroGeo Sphere equips it with scientific evidence.
details:
AgroGeo Sphere is an Earth-observation agricultural decision-support prototype focused on Jaranwala, Punjab, Pakistan. It helps users compare crop-rotation scenarios, explore seasonal conditions and understand how water, soil and crop choices influence sustainable farming.

Users enter field information, review seasonal NDVI, rainfall and temperature trends, and compare rotations such as wheat–Kharif fodder, wheat–Kharif pulses and wheat–fallow–wheat. The Precision Lab uses adjustable weighted criteria for water suitability, seasonal fit, soil cover, nutrient-cycling potential and entered soil properties. Missing criteria are excluded and score coverage is displayed. Three.js renders interactive 3D crop-growth comparisons, while CropMaster AI uses GPT-5.2 through an API endpoint to explain results, with an offline fallback.

Our research workbook records Jaranwala’s 2020–21 reported area as 444,249 acres, net sown area as 368,418 acres and total cropped area as 491,313 acres (133.36% cropping intensity). It also documents Faisalabad District rotation examples and specifications for Landsat, NASA GPM IMERG, NASA POWER and SMAP.

The project was developed primarily with no-code/low-code tools: Claude for the website foundation, Power Query and Excel for data extraction and analysis, Three.js for 3D interface development, and ChatGPT for brainstorming and AI integration.

Our originality lies in combining local agricultural evidence, an editable rotation-scoring simulator, interactive 3D visualisation and AI explanations in one platform. We considered data reliability, spatial scale, usability and scientific limitations. Satellite time-series values are not yet extracted for individual fields; demonstration data and generic assumptions are labelled. The intended impact is to support better-informed, climate-aware farm planning—not replace local agronomists or guarantee yields.
